title: Verifier‑Grounded Paired Evaluation of Intent→Config Generation (Estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; preregistered generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate)
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that tests the preregistered estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under the frozen generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate. Using N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), the deterministic template baseline passed the verifier on 120/120 tasks and the LLM condition (declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini) also passed on 120/120 tasks. Paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We (1) publish the complete execution and analysis artifacts with SHA‑256 fingerprints required for byte‑for‑byte reproduction (see execution/execution_manifest.json in the artifact bundle), (2) show—using those same archived artifacts—why the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced a degenerate paired contingency (identical canonical candidate reused per pair + deterministic validator), and (3) provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory design, validator diversification) that preserve reproducibility while answering the operational question practitioners typically need (independent generative reliability). Representative archived files used in our diagnosis include analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 9f25790c7eeaafb3...), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 9c77c96f37c4b6f...), execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...), and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...).

sections.introduction: Translating high‑level operator intent into correct device configuration is a safety‑critical NetOps task: transient misordering or missing steps can break reachability, violate ACLs, or produce unsafe transient states. Deterministic offline validators (reachability/ACL/routing analyzers in the Batfish family and successors) are operational oracles for pre‑deployment checks. Our preregistered study asks a precisely specified estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate. This estimand tests whether a deterministic validator returns different pass/fail outcomes when an identical canonical candidate is scored under two named conditions (baseline template vs. LLM‑generated guarded condition). That estimand differs from the operational question many practitioners ask—namely, the independent per‑condition probability that an LLM, sampled independently, will produce a verifier‑passing configuration. We execute the preregistered pipeline, publish the exhaustive artifacts, report the exact confirmatory counts and inferential outputs from the archived traces, and diagnose artifactically why the confirmatory contrast collapsed to a degenerate contingency.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded workflows and generate–validate–repair architectures are a common operational pattern in NetOps and in recent LLM→configuration research. Tooling such as Batfish demonstrates high‑fidelity configuration analysis and has been used to validate forwarding/ACL invariants at scale. Recent LLM‑driven NetOps literature varies in sampling semantics (single‑candidate vs. independent per‑condition or multi‑seed) and repair budgets; those methodological choices materially change what is being measured (validator determinism vs. independent generative reliability). We position our artifact release and design diagnosis as complementary to prior work that emphasizes independent sampling and bounded repair, by showing how preregistered generation semantics determine the estimand and how exhaustive artifact publication resolves inferential ambiguity.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. We preregistered CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1 prior to any model calls (SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37). Key preregistered elements: N = 120 paired tasks (40 per topology class), declared_model_version gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5, primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, analysis engine paired_binary_analysis_v1 with 10,000 bootstrap resamples (seed = 1729), and preregistered generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate. Task synthesis. Tasks were programmatically generated from deterministic templates (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit required_sequence, per‑task workflow_policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups), and difficulty annotations. Representative task artifact: execution/task_manifest.jsonl and the concrete canonical candidate for pair 000001 archived at execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8be...). Model and orchestration. The declared model and adapter are recorded in execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 a40e96e2...). Generation semantics. Per preregistration we generated one canonical candidate per pair (shared_initial_candidate) and reused that identical candidate for both baseline and guarded scoring episodes; the shared candidate files are archived under execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt. Validator and scoring. The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0) enforces required_sequences, transient safety policies, and final_state invariants; each scoring episode emits a JSON trace archived at execution/scoring/*.json (example: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...). Statistical plan. Primary estimator = mean_i (guarded_i − baseline_i) over the 120 pairs; inference via 10,000‑resample percentile bootstrap (seed 1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test on the paired 2×2 contingency. Contamination and reproducibility. We ran preregistered string‑overlap contamination heuristics and recorded results (analysis/contamination_summary.csv) and we publish full provider call traces and call_cache artifacts to enable independent exposure analyses. All files and SHA‑256 fingerprints are listed in execution/execution_manifest.json.
sections.results: Confirmatory counts and preregistered inference. All preregistered confirmatory episodes completed and are archived. Results: baseline_success_count = 120/120; guarded_success_count (gpt‑5‑mini, shared_initial seed_0) = 120/120; complete_pair_count = 120. The paired contingency is n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c7eeaafb3...). Primary estimand: paired difference = 0.00. Bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Representative per‑episode artifacts supporting these numbers: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...). Why the paired contingency is degenerate. The preregistered generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate produced one canonical LLM candidate per task and the harness reused that identical candidate for both baseline and guarded scoring episodes. Because the validator is deterministic and the task templates contain explicit required_sequences that the canonical candidate satisfied, identical inputs yield identical pass/fail outcomes; the logged validator traces (execution/scoring/*.json) deterministically link candidate bytes to the scoring result. This artifact‑visible causal chain explains the degenerate contingency (n_11 = 120) and therefore why the confirmatory paired result does not estimate independent generative reliability. Runnable modifications. The same archived pipeline supports deterministic reruns answering the operational question: (A) independent_per_condition confirmatory rerun (generate distinct seed per condition per task), (B) multi‑seed per‑condition execution (K ≥ 3 seeds), and (C) validator diversification (run multiple independent validators and report intersection/union pass rates). All rerun inputs and validator binaries are referenced by SHA in the manifest to ensure byte‑for‑byte reproducibility.
sections.discussion: Interpretation and correct inference. The reported confirmatory statistics are internally valid for the preregistered estimand (validator response to identical canonical candidates). They are not evidence about independent LLM sampling reliability; conflating these would be a category error. Methodological lesson: preregistered generation semantics determine estimands; exhaustive artifact publication is required to diagnose regressions and to enable deterministic, informative reruns. Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared_initial semantics intentionally removed generation variance and thus cannot test independent reliability. Construct validity: template‑aligned tasks plus a single deterministic validator increase the chance canonical candidates pass. External validity: a single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) and synthetic tasks limit generalizability to other models and natural intents. Contamination: preregistered heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds but overlap heuristics are imperfect proxies for pretraining exposure. Operational implications. For deployment decisions operators should estimate independent per‑condition pass probabilities via independent sampling, multi‑seed replication, and validator ensembles. Our artifact bundle makes those reruns deterministic and immediately executable for practitioners and auditors.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and published the complete artifact bundle that permits byte‑for‑byte reproduction. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics both baseline and LLM guarded conditions passed the deterministic validator on all N = 120 tasks (both 120/120). The archived artifacts show explicitly why the paired contingency is degenerate (identical canonical candidate per pair + deterministic validator). We provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed replication, validator diversification) that preserve reproducibility while producing informative independent comparisons relevant to deployment. All execution and analysis artifacts, the preregistration SHA‑256, and the immutable master prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) are included in the submission bundle to enable exact audit and follow‑up experiments.

The paper’s conclusions are explicitly bounded by the preregistered estimand and by limitations discussed in the manuscript.
limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not part of the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
